site: iCIMS and ATS portals using HTMLInputElement submit controls (Mutual of Enumclaw)
class: SubmissionGuardV0 credentialControl and candidateProfileControl checked element.matches('button,[role=button]') which rejected <input type='submit'> elements, preventing profile and account creation
symptom: On Mutual of Enumclaw (iCIMS), 'Submit Profile' rendered as <input type='submit' value='Submit Profile'> instead of a <button> tag. Although valid credentials and emails were populated, SubmissionGuardV0.click_candidate_profile returned False with ACCOUNT_CREATE_BLOCKED: account-control click was not confirmed.
root_cause: 1. submission_guard.py's candidateProfileControl and credentialControl used `element.matches('button,[role=button]')`. In DOM CSS selector rules, `button` matches only HTMLButtonElement, so HTMLInputElement (such as <input type='submit'> or <input type='button'>) evaluated to false and failed authorization. 2. Companion and click event listeners only checked `element instanceof HTMLButtonElement`.
why_tests_missed: f198 tests used `<button type='submit'>Submit Profile</button>`, which passed `button,[role=button]`, whereas iCIMS production pages use `<input type='submit' value='Submit Profile'>`.
fix: In submission_guard.py, expand control tag matching to `element.matches('button, input[type=submit], input[type=button], [role=button]')`, and allow HTMLInputElement in authorized companion clicks.
prevention: Whenever matching action controls by tag/role in DOM guards, include both HTMLButtonElement and HTMLInputElement submit controls.
